newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL shares end weak on Dow fear, regional switching.
newsitem.headline: KL shares end weak on Dow fear, regional switching.

text.p: Fears of a volatile Wall Street and recommendations by some large international brokerages to switch out of Malaysia depressed blue chip share prices on Monday, analysts and dealers said.
The benchmark Composite Index of 100 large-capitalised stocks ended 8.44 points lower at 1,234.03, while the all-share EMAS index, closed 2.83 points down at 361.75.
"There's definitely volatility in the U.S. market, as it is getting worried over an interest rate rise," said Tony Shue, an institutional dealer at Jupiter Securities.

"We are tracking the perceived performance of the Dow. People have lost interest in the market in anticipation of the Federal Open Market Committee meeting on March 25," said Soh Meng Hui, research manager at K.L. City Securities.

"Some international houses are recommending that investors switch out of Malaysia into Thailand as their political stability seems to be returning, and P.E.'s (price earnings multiples) here are looking a bit expensive," said Soh.
Retail interest continued to dominate the market, analysts said.
"Institutions are still not in the market," said Soh.
